purpose: Durable visual-authority, continuity, and sequential-production contract for Division Threshold image production.

authority.storyUnit: The exact assembled RexPrompt recipe controls what happens on the current page.
authority.releasedVisualCanon: StarSplitterVisions main controls released canon when Division Threshold is released there. The series is currently unreleased.
authority.currentProduction: Approved scoped references and approved recipe-level production drafts may establish visual state at their stated scope. Failed, rejected, repeated, superseded, promotional-without-reference-scope, or merely generated images are not continuity authority.
authority.immediateContinuity: The immediately preceding approved page may establish carried state, but it is never the sole identity, world, or style reference.

textualProductionBaseline.rule: Textual anchors supplement the approved visual references and protect details that are unclear visually; they do not authorize redesigning an established approved appearance.

characterIdentity.primary: Use the approved character references in production/references/division-threshold/visual-reference-pack.json for Ostra-9, Axiom, Nico-14, John Mercer, Nathan Price, and Kellen Cartwright.
characterIdentity.support: Use assembler-visible visual anchors, performance notes, and continuity locks to protect details not legible in the reference image.
characterIdentity.rule: A newly generated appearance does not replace an established reference merely because it is newer.

worldAndLocation.primary: Use the assembled page setting/settingText, region/regionText, and faction context together with persistent shelves and applicable approved page references.
worldAndLocation.rule: Recurring locations retain one visual identity across camera changes.

storyPageLanguage.primary: Use dt-e001-p05-production-example from the visual-reference pack as the approved early-Issue-1 page-language and Stack-atmosphere anchor.
preserve: clear panel hierarchy and readable story beats
lived-in layered Stack infrastructure rather than generic cyberpunk
restrained integrated civic signage and lettering
established Division Threshold palette, rendering density, and architectural texture
exclude: failed, rejected, repeated or superseded generations

currentProduction.rule: Recipe-level approved drafts establish post-start story state; visual-reference assets do not by themselves advance the sequential production frontier.

sessionStart: Resolve the requested issue and ordered RexPrompt recipes from the current repository.
Check StarSplitterVisions main for any released Division Threshold baseline.
Load production/references/division-threshold/visual-reference-pack.json and select only the references relevant to the upcoming pages.
Resolve approved recipe-level drafts from production/drafts/manifest.json.
For every recurring character or recurring location required by the next page, use an actual approved visual reference whenever one exists.
Derive the production frontier from released pages plus approved recipe-level drafts and explicit current user direction; do not use a remembered cursor.
perPage: Retrieve or assemble the exact current RexPrompt page recipe.
Identify every recurring character, location, costume, prop, and carried story state required by the recipe.
Select the applicable approved visual references from the Division Threshold visual-reference pack.
Inspect the immediately preceding approved page when spatial, physical, emotional, environmental, or object state carries forward.
Generate only after recipe, visual references, and immediate continuity are resolved.
Preserve exact dialogue ownership and the page's required final beat.

frontierPolicy.rule: Visual references establish visual authority but do not substitute for recipe-level completion. The production frontier is the first ordered scripted page without released canon or an approved production draft, subject to explicit current user instruction and clearly established approvals.

storyPageOutputRule: A normal scripted Division Threshold unit is a finished full-color portrait prestige science-fiction comic page. Do not add a series title, issue header, page label, character name/handle label, dossier frame, credits, promotional callout, infographic heading, or other non-scripted text. Only text required by the assembled recipe belongs on the story page.
